sections.html:
With a median owner-occupied value of $551,200 and owners who tend to stay put, a standard listing is the usual route when a house is in good shape. A cash buyer is more useful when the house needs work that would take months to finish, when a probate or move deadline is close, or when you want to avoid showings.

Park Ridge is a city in Cook County about 15 miles north of downtown Chicago, close to O'Hare International Airport. Population is 38,463, and much of the housing dates to the mid-century boom, so a buyer's inspector will look closely at the age of the wiring, plumbing, roof and foundation.

With 84.8 percent of homes owner-occupied, most buyers are families who plan to live in the house and who usually rely on a mortgage. A house that cannot pass a lender's appraisal or an inspection can lose that kind of buyer, which is where a cash sale enters the picture.

Houses here sell at prices where small defects matter to a lender. If the roof is near the end of its life or the electrical panel is original, a mortgage buyer may ask for credits or walk away, while an investor will simply lower the offer and close without a financing step. Decide which of those outcomes you can live with before you set your asking price.

sections.h2: The Park Ridge transfer tax and who files it
sections.html:
The city charges its own real estate transfer tax, and the seller pays it. The rate is $2.00 per $1,000 of value or fraction thereof, and the fee for an exempt transfer is $25.00.

To get the transfer tax certificate, send the Finance Department:

  • The PTAX-203 or MyDec form.
  • A photo of the water meter for the final reading.
  • The closing date.
  • A contact name, phone number and email address.

Documents go to transferstamp@parkridge.us or to the Finance Department at 505 Butler Place. Questions go to 847-318-5222, option 4. The certificate is issued once the tax and any other amounts owed to the city, including the final water bill, are paid, and it is attached to the deed at recording. On top of the city's tax, recording adds the state's 50 cents per $500 and the county's 25 cents per $500.

Closing cannot be completed without the certificate and the final water reading, so ask your closing attorney or title company to start these steps as soon as the contract is signed.

Water is billed every other month, issued on the last day of the month and due by the 20th. Email the meter photo no earlier than five days before closing, with the service address and closing date. Water is not shut off during a transfer, and the account moves automatically into the buyer's name.

Final payment is accepted as cash, credit or debit card, certified check, money order or attorney's check. Homeowners are responsible for repairs to the water service pipe between the buffalo box and the house, so a leak that turns up in a buyer's inspection is yours to fix or to credit.

Assessment is a Cook County function, so property tax appeals and exemptions go to the county assessor, not City Hall.

sections.h2: Do you need a permit for repairs on a Park Ridge house?
sections.html:
A permit is required for most construction. The city lists new buildings, additions, garages, driveways, HVAC, electrical and plumbing work, pools, fences, patios, decks, sheds and siding. No permit is needed for window replacement unless the opening is enlarged, or for residential roof replacement, although roofing contractors must hold a city license. Routine maintenance that leaves existing systems and structural walls alone also needs none.

Timing matters if you plan fixes before a sale:

  • Reviews usually take up to two weeks, and the standard time is two weeks for every permit during the May to September busy season.
  • Residential permits stay valid for one year, and a renewal after expiration costs 50 percent of the original permit fee.
  • Applications go through the Civic Access online portal, and inspections are booked by morning or afternoon block with a one to two business day lead time.

Questions go to the Community Preservation and Development department at 847-318-5291. A separate tree removal permit is required for trees larger than 10 inches in diameter, so check before clearing a lot.

Park Ridge has a Historic Preservation Commission. A house becomes a local landmark only with the owner's consent, and a designation can be rescinded, though the Commission encourages owners to look at alternatives first. If your house is already landmarked, tell buyers early.

Park Ridge also sits close to O'Hare, and buyers sometimes ask about the neighborhood as a result. Be ready to talk about the block, the two Metra stops (Park Ridge and Dee Road, on the Union Pacific Northwest Line) and which school your street feeds, since families make up most of the buyers here. Park Ridge-Niles School District 64 runs the elementary schools and Maine Township High School District 207 serves high school students.

If you are unsure whether your address carries a designation, ask the Community Preservation and Development department before you list, so the answer is ready when a buyer asks.

sections.h2: A simple order of steps for a Park Ridge sale
sections.html:
Whichever way you sell, the same few tasks set the closing date. If you do them early, nothing stalls at the last minute, and the buyer's side has less to chase.

  1. Decide between a listing and a cash offer by comparing what each would net after repairs and carrying costs.
  2. Check for open permits and tell your buyer about any past work that needed one.
  3. Once the contract is signed, have your attorney or title company send the transfer tax paperwork to the Finance Department.
  4. Email the water meter photo within five days of closing.
  5. Pay the transfer tax and any remaining city amounts so the certificate can be issued and attached to the deed.

A cash buyer who accepts the house as is makes the repair step disappear, so the city paperwork becomes the main work left before closing. Keep copies of everything you file, since the title company will ask for the certificate number on closing day.

faqs.q: How much is the Park Ridge transfer tax?
faqs.a: The city charges $2.00 per $1,000 of value or fraction thereof, paid by the seller. The state adds 50 cents per $500 and the county adds 25 cents per $500.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay my final water bill before closing in Park Ridge?
faqs.a: Yes. The transfer tax certificate is issued after the tax and any other amounts owed to the city, including the final water bill, are paid. Email a photo of the meter to the Finance Department no earlier than five days before closing.

faqs.q: Can I replace my roof or windows in Park Ridge without a permit?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Residential roof replacement and window replacement do not need a permit unless the window opening is enlarged. Roofing contractors must hold a city license, and decks, fences and electrical work still require permits.

faqs.q: Who handles Park Ridge property tax appeals?
faqs.a: The county does, not the city. Assessment is a county function, so owners go to the Cook County Assessor's office for appeals, exemptions and the required forms.

faqs.q: Does the water account transfer when a Park Ridge house sells?
faqs.a: Yes. The city places the account in the buyer's name automatically, does not shut off service during the transfer, and bills every other month afterward. Sellers settle the final reading through the transfer tax process.
